## Scope

`base` (99cc3680) → HEAD (6d018934), one commit, `fix(review): reduce CodeRabbit pause friction` — 16 files, 213 non-test changed lines. Worktree clean apart from untracked `.skill/`. Ran `pr-ready-state.test.mjs` (82 pass) and `pr-feedback-state.test.mjs` (51 pass); ran the second-model side channel (`codex-review.sh base`, report at `.reviews/codex-review-20260827-210528.md`).

---

## 1. Hold for one check — nothing may ever reach `reviewed`

`scripts/pr/pr-ready-state-core.mjs:759-770`

`reviewed` has exactly one route: a CodeRabbit **review record** whose body matches `**Run ID**` *and* whose commit oid equals the head. Both halves rest on assumptions with no captured payload behind them in this repo.

**(a) The clean-run body.** The repo's only real CodeRabbit captures — `scripts/pr/pr-feedback-state.test.mjs:3355-3373`, commented "the shapes observed on PR #1918, the first PR CodeRabbit reviewed in this repo" — put the clean-run completion text (`"No actionable comments were generated in the recent review. 🎉"`, line 3369) in the **top-level walkthrough issue comment**, which carries no Run ID. The new issue-comment loop at `:772-784` only matches the agent's own request marker; it never inspects CodeRabbit-authored comments. The change's own fixture (`pr-ready-state.test.mjs:2226-2229`) is the *with-findings* shape, `Actionable comments posted: 1`.

**(b) The commit oid.** `isCurrentReviewSignal` (`:657-658`) takes the oid branch whenever `currentHeadOid` is set, and it always is (`:875`, from `pr.headRefOid`). `pr.reviews` is passed straight through from `gh pr view --json reviews` (`scripts/pr/pr-ready-state.mjs:770`) with no enrichment. If gh's `reviews` field carries no commit, `reviewCommitOid` returns null and `reviewed` is unreachable whatever the body says.

**Consequence if either holds:** every PR reads `stale`/`missing`, and the closeout rule posts `@coderabbitai review` on PRs CodeRabbit already reviewed cleanly — spending the Pro+ ladder round the ADR change exists to save.

**Confidence: suspected, not confirmed.** `gh` is disabled in this checkout, so I could not observe a real payload. One command on a live PR with a clean run settles both halves:

```
gh pr view <n> --repo <BASE_REPO> --json reviews \
  --jq '.reviews[] | {keys: keys, body: .body[0:200]}'
```

**Remedy:** capture that payload as a fixture before merging. If completion lands in the walkthrough comment, extend the issue-comment loop to accept a CodeRabbit-authored walkthrough at the current head. If reviews lack a commit oid, enrich them rather than leaning on the existing helper.

## 2. Follow-up — the request marker is accepted from any author

`scripts/pr/pr-ready-state-core.mjs:772-784` — no author or association check. The sibling marker parser `parseReadinessOverrideComment` (`:523-556`) requires a trusted human via `HUMAN_OVERRIDE_ASSOCIATIONS`, and `issue-board-backfill.mjs:90` uses `TRUSTED_ASSOCIATIONS`; this path uses neither. Anyone who copies the public head SHA into the marker flips the state to `requested`, and the runbook (`docs/notes/pr-ready-state.md:398-401`, `.claude/skills/babysit-pr/SKILL.md:308-310`) then forbids the authorized request for that head. Consequence is a silently skipped advisory review, not a false ready — the gate is `required: false` and is outside the readiness AND at `pr-feedback-state-core.mjs:543-547`. Confirmed by reading. Reuse the existing trusted-association helper.

## 3. Follow-up — watchlist drift, and the watchlist is now stale

`scripts/pr/pr-ready-state-core.mjs` goes 889 → 961 rough lines (998 → 1,077 raw), while `docs/notes/file-size-watch.md:53` still records `888 | 993 | soft cap`. Policy at `docs/pr-checklists/recurring-review-patterns.md:191-194`: don't append to a file already drifting up. This will **not** fail CI — the same policy records that `scripts/` has no eslint `max-lines`, so the watchlist report is the only signal. (The second-model report called this a 1,000-line hard-cap crossing; that's measured on raw lines. The governing metric is `rough`, and 961 stays under.) Confirmed by counting.

## 4. Preference — documented JSON sample now incomplete

`docs/notes/pr-ready-state.md:275-296` still shows four gates. The same file's new prose (`:111-127`, `:351-356`) tells the reader the projection exposes `codeRabbitReviewSignal`. An agent treating the sample as the contract won't see it.

---

## Considered and cleared

- The agent's own `@coderabbitai review` comment does **not** become a feedback blocker — `pr-feedback-state-core.mjs:210` gates actionability on `isReviewBotComment`, which lists bot logins only.
- Terminal PRs don't emit `undefined`: `terminalGates` (`:628-633`) and `summarizeTerminalReadyState` (`:828`) both got the key, and `pr-ready-state.test.mjs:2104-2107` asserts it.
- `.agents/skills/` and `.claude/skills/` copies are byte-identical (all three files diffed) — the mirror stayed in step.
- No stale `auto_pause_after_reviewed_commits: 2` anywhere; config, pin test and ADR agree on 5. The 2 → 5 change itself: no defect found.
- The `pr-ready-state.md` 8/9/10 renumber breaks no cross-reference — `pr-operating-card.md:189`'s "step 8" indexes the card's own list.
- No flat `scripts/pr-*-state-*.mjs` duplicates survive the D3 migration, so no sibling copy is left on old semantics.
- `git diff --check` clean; no tab-indented additions; no conflict markers.

## What I could not do

- **`gh` is disabled here.** No claim about live GitHub payload shape could be confirmed — that is the entire basis of finding 1's uncertainty.
- **`scripts/coderabbit-config.test.mjs` could not run** — `js-yaml` is not installed. The YAML change was read, not executed; the config pin is unverified coverage, not a clean bill.
- The two suites that did pass run over hand-written fixtures that encode the very assumptions finding 1 questions. Green here is not evidence the classifier works against real CodeRabbit output.

**Proof still owed:** one real clean-run CodeRabbit payload and one real `reviews` record from a live PR; the config pin test with dependencies installed; one end-to-end closeout before trusting the rule not to double-request.

## Verdict

No **confirmed** must-fix, so this doesn't get a blocking verdict from me. But the change's whole value proposition rests on the unverified assumption in finding 1, and if it's wrong the change costs review rounds instead of saving them. I'd hold the merge for the one `gh` command above. Findings 2-4 are non-blocking.

The second-model pass independently surfaced 1(a) and 2 and returned BLOCK; I confirmed both against the repo before adopting them, corrected its metric on 3, and did not adopt its suggested `recent_review_start`/`recent_review_end` markers — those appear nowhere in this repo's captures.
other_review:
The exact-head classifier mishandles two CodeRabbit comment paths. Untrusted markers can suppress a legitimate request, while completed clean top-level reviews remain invisible and cause redundant reviews.

Full review comments:

- [P2] Reject request markers from untrusted commenters — /Users/chapati/.cache/mento-review-eval/fx-1990-6d0189349a48/scripts/pr/pr-ready-state-core.mjs:772-774
  Because this is a public repository, outside users can post PR comments. This loop does not inspect `author_association` or login before turning a matching marker into `requested`. An outside comment that quotes the documented command and current SHA therefore suppresses the trusted closeout request for that head, even when CodeRabbit does not honor the outsider's command. Restrict request markers to OWNER, MEMBER, COLLABORATOR, or recognized agent bots so the [one-request contract](.agents/skills/babysit-pr/SKILL.md#L310-L312) cannot be bypassed.

- [P2] Recognize successful top-level CodeRabbit runs — /Users/chapati/.cache/mento-review-eval/fx-1990-6d0189349a48/scripts/pr/pr-ready-state-core.mjs:772-774
  When CodeRabbit completes a clean run by editing its top-level `recent_review_start`/`recent_review_end` summary, its GitHub review record can remain empty. This issue-comment pass ignores that completed run because it accepts only manual-request bodies. The signal remains `missing` or `stale`, so closeout spends a second review despite the exact head already being clean. Recognize a trusted clean-run block only when it has a Run ID, a full commit range ending at the current head, and `updated_at >= headUpdatedAt`; this preserves the [one-request contract](.agents/skills/babysit-pr/SKILL.md#L310-L312).
